title: SDK Connector Priority Canvas: token rotation, language parity, and streaming ergonomics for regulated customers
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures an intake and prioritization canvas for a cluster of customer requests about SDK/client connector behavior for regulated enterprise customers. The focus areas are: (1) standardized token rotation and short-lived credentials patterns; (2) language parity across priority client bindings (Python, TypeScript, Java, Go); and (3) streaming ergonomics for resumable sessions and idempotent reconnections. Customers asking for this include two regulated banks and an e-pharma partner who require predictable auth rotation, auditable token exchange flows, and robust streaming reconnect semantics for long-running document processing jobs.

Context and problem statement:
- Several enterprise onramps stalled during security review due to unclear guidance on token rotation and refresh semantics for server-to-server and delegated user flows.
- Engineering feedback: implementing 6 language bindings with inconsistent auth shims has created maintenance overhead and platform support burden.
- Product feedback: lack of clear client-side reconnection/resume semantics for streaming causes customer FTR (failed to recover) incidents during long-lived sessions when corporate proxies rotate connections.

Objective:
Produce a prioritized, implementable plan (playbook + minimal SDK prototypes) to:
  * Standardize token rotation patterns (recommended: short-lived service tokens + refresh via secure token-exchange endpoint, with example flows for OAuth2 refresh, mTLS client cert rotation, and SAML assertion exchange).
  * Define language parity targets and a minimal feature set that each official binding must meet for GA enterprise onboarding.
  * Define streaming contract changes: session-resume token, sequence-number idempotency, and graceful server-driven fallback to polling for long-hanging jobs.

Success metrics:
  * Reduce 'security gating' incidents in sales cycle by 80% for targeted customers within 3 months of playbook publication.
  * Implement SDK feature parity for core auth flows across 4 languages within 2 sprints of approval.
  * Demo a streaming resume flow in the demo app with a <500ms median reconnect handshake for normal reconnects and robust resume for transient 30-120s network interruptions.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence with diagrams for server-to-server and delegated flows and sample curl + SDK snippets
Prototype SDK adapter (TS + Python) implementing recommended token-exchange pattern with integration test against staging KMS/oauth-mock
Language parity checklist defined and signed off by SDK owners for Python, TS, Java, Go
Streaming spec with sequence-number idempotency and resume token documented and implemented in streaming proxy (ENG-2087) tests
Security review packet prepared and uploaded to compliance with threat model and FIPS/KMS mapping
comments: 2026-02-11 | Maya Thompson: Initial intake from AE team + security. Collected three customer ask decks; requested an architecture sketch from ENG for token refresh options.
2026-02-17 | Diego Ruiz: Prioritized token rotation and streaming resume as P1 items given sales risk. Proposed minimal implementation: token-exchange proxy + SDK helpers, not full OAuth library.
2026-02-23 | Priya Nair (Security): Flagged SAML-backed delegated flows require explicit audit trail. Requested we include KMS key identifiers and rotation cadence in playbook.

2026-03-03 | Evan Park (Engineering): Posted draft solution for token-exchange endpoint (ENG-3021). Notes: prefer JWT-based short-lived tokens (TTL 15m) and optional refresh via mTLS for private deployments.

2026-03-07 | Diego Ruiz: Design review with SDK owners. Agreed: TS and Python prototypes first; add Java and Go in parallel but lower cadence. Decided to implement a small shim library instead of changing core runtime authentication logic.
2026-03-09 | Legal (Jonas Reed): Request that examples avoid embedded secrets and show proper rotation; asked for standard language around liability and customer-managed key guidance.

2026-03-12 | Maya Thompson: Added acceptance criteria and wireframe links; scheduled demo for 2026-03-25 with Sales/SEs and the two POC customers. Requested ENG to allocate 3 dev days for prototype stabilization.
decisions: Adopt short-lived JWTs (TTL 15m) issued by token-exchange proxy as default server-to-server pattern for hosted and dedicated deployments.
Provide SDK helper library (small shim) that implements rotation and transparent refreshing; language-specific ergonomics remain the team's responsibility but must satisfy parity checklist.
Streaming resume will use a resume-token + last-applied-sequence-number handshake; server will provide tombstone window semantics for eventual consistency.
For Private deployments with FIPS/KMS requirements, document alternate flow using signed assertions and customer-managed HSM integration; do not block GA for hosted flow.
next_steps: ENG: Finalize token-exchange proxy API and open implementation RFC (owner: Evan Park, ENG-3021).
DX: Draft two SDK prototypes (TypeScript, Python) with example apps and integration tests against oauth-mock (owners: Priya S., Alex G.).
Security: Prepare security review packet and run tabletop with compliance (owner: Priya Nair).
PM: Run demo with SEs and POC customers on 2026-03-25 and capture acceptance feedback; iterate on playbook based on feedback.
